summary: Phase 7 can falsely claim the knowledge index was updated after a failed append, which defeats the persistence guarantee and makes later cross-reference behavior silently incomplete.

findings.title: Append failure can be reported as a successful index write
findings.description: The append-failure path only prints an error and then continues into the tail-based verification. If the user chose 'Keep both' for an existing duplicate, or if the last existing record already has the same dedup_key, a failed append can still pass the LAST_DEDUP_KEY check and allow Step 7.6 to report success even though the new entry was never persisted. The verification also checks only dedup_key, not the new entry id or full serialized record, so it cannot distinguish the intended write from an older same-key line.
findings.recommendation: Make append failure terminal (exit 1/return nonzero) before any read-back check, gate Step 7.6 on an explicit success flag, and verify the last line matches the new entry's unique id or full JSON hash in addition to dedup_key.

next_steps: Make append failure terminal and verify new entry's unique id in the read-back check.
